notes: Pirate scouts, salvagers, haulers and tankers pulled into a battle now fight back with normal pirate tactics. They no longer break off on the first tick, so you can fight and destroy them.
A pirate support ship that does escape a battle now leaves the system. It no longer stays at the same spot and drops straight back into a new battle.
Faction mobile bases can now jump to any adjacent public system, even if the commander has never visited it.
Jumps to frontier systems still need the commander or the faction to have charted the destination. The `unknown_system` error now says this.
Fixed a frontier planet that could not be reached because it shared an id with a POI in another system. The planet has a new id and name.
While a faction's recruitment office upgrade is under construction, the faction keeps the member cap of the office's current tier. Before, the cap fell to the default until the upgrade finished.

The `faction_garages` help now says who can claim a prestige hull from a faction garage: a member who holds its personal achievement, a member whose faction holds its faction achievement, or the faction leader for a leader-only hull. Other members get `not_qualified`.
Station facilities now count as supplied when storage covers what they draw each cycle. You no longer need the full listed upkeep on hand; topping up a few units at a time keeps them running.
A facility that runs short comes back online at the next cycle once at least one of each missing item is in storage. It is not charged for the cycles it was offline.

Life-support and power status items now show `average_burn_per_cycle`, and `facility types` and reported facility upkeep show `maintenance_average_burn_per_cycle`: the units actually drawn per 100-tick cycle. The life-support block also lists which items a short plant is missing.
NPC stations now budget their upkeep at what their facilities really burn.
Wildlife no longer attacks a ship on the tick it arrives at a location, by jump, wormhole or in-system travel. You always get one command (move on, cloak, hunt) before a leviathan there can strike.

Leviathans no longer flee the moment a hunting fleet jumps into their system. They now judge traffic over about an hour and avoid only systems that stay busy, so a fleet that arrives can find and fight them.
Young leviathans no longer bolt the instant a ship reaches their location or a battle starts in their system. They can still slip away from ships or fights that linger.
Customs cutters now carry warp scramblers and hold the pilot they inspect until the cargo scan ends. You get a `hold_update` notification with `source: "customs"`.
Evading a customs inspection is now a crime in that empire: `customs_evasion_policed_space`.
If customs seizes your contraband, the cutter sends you a private receipt that lists each seized stack and its value, the fine assessed and the fine collected. Then you go on your way.
Every customs inspection now goes in your action log as `combat.customs_inspection`, with its outcome and any bounty.
Warp core stabilizers are stronger: each one now cancels 2 disruption points, so one stabilizer beats one warp scrambler in battle or in a player's toll or scan hold.

Pirate raids now remember where their ships were destroyed. A stronghold steers its raids around systems where it recently lost several ships, skips targets in those systems, and stays home when no safe route is left. The memory fades over a few days.
When pirates judge whether a station is too well defended to raid, they now count the owner's and its allies' ships anywhere in the system, docked or not.
Faction mobile bases are no longer raid targets.

Every battle now calls in each side's faction and mutual allies who are undocked anywhere in the system. Allies that set `ally_battle_opt_out` stay out. This now applies when a faction station is attacked or raided, when police or an empire fleet engage a pilot, when a drone attacks, and when you join a fight with `battle engage`. A pilot who has left a battle is not called back into it.
Pirate raids on a faction station now call the owner's faction and mutual allies from anywhere in the system, not only ships at the station.

Pirates now fight as a stronghold: when one is in a battle, every ship of its stronghold in the system joins. Haulers, salvagers, scouts and tankers join too and try to flee, so a raid's cargo train can now be shot in the battle. Pirates of another stronghold are not allies: they do not join, and they do not come to defend.

Unpaid rent no longer repossesses facilities. A facility that owes rent stays yours but stops working (no production, services, or bonuses) until the arrears are paid. Storage, fuel bunkers, and ship garages keep working.

Rent amnesty: every facility the station repossessed for unpaid rent has been returned to its previous owner or faction, free, and all unpaid rent arrears are forgiven. Check your action log for `rent_amnesty` and `facility_restored` entries.
Inactive owners no longer build up rent arrears, the same way inactive players pay no weekly taxes. A faction builds none while no member is active.
You cannot transfer or sell a facility while it owes rent.
Rent warnings now arrive at the first missed cycle and then once a day. The `grace_cycles` and `eviction_grace_cycles` fields and the `facility_reclaimed` notification are removed.
The pirate radio Discord channel now posts one message when a raid wrecks a station, not two.
Passive Engineering XP has a new rule. You earn 1 XP per tick while you are online and your fitted modules draw 90% or more of your ship's power capacity or CPU capacity.
The rule uses the module draw before the Engineering discount. A higher Engineering level no longer moves a full fit below the line, and a fit that is full on CPU now counts.

`get_ship` has two new fields, `module_cpu` and `module_power`: the draw of your fitted modules before the Engineering discount. Compare them to `cpu_capacity` and `power_capacity`. `cpu_used` and `power_used` are unchanged and still show the draw after the discount.
Pilots who are logged out no longer earn passive Engineering XP.
Something new has moved into Nyx Nexus Station. Listen to the pirate radio around GSC-0008, and scan anything unusual near Overlord Nyx.
One account can now hold up to 4 WebSocket connections at once. For example, a script and the web client can play the same account together. A new connection no longer closes the old one.
Close code `4001` (`session_replaced`) now means the account opened a fifth connection, and the oldest one was closed.
Every connection receives every server push. The one-action-per-tick limit stays per player: if one connection has an action pending, a mutation from another gets `action_pending`.

Send a `request_id` with every mutation. The answers go only to the connection that sent it. The other connections on the same protocol version receive the `action_result` with no `request_id`, as a state change that carries the command's name.
Market and observation subscriptions are per player. An unsubscribe from one connection ends the updates for all of them. The player goes offline when the last connection closes.
`station set_gate_access` now accepts `access: "allies"`. Your faction and its allied factions can cross the gate. Allies pay the toll, and all other pilots are refused.
Gate status now has `allies_only: true` when a gate is set to allies.

The public economy report (`/api/economy`) now includes `current.wallet_age`: total player wallet credits grouped by how long since the owner last issued a command (<1 day to 90+ days), with account count and share per group. NPC accounts are excluded.

`facility` actions `list`, `owned` and `faction_owned` now report `ticks_until_complete` for your own and your faction's facilities while they are under construction. The text status reads `building (N ticks left)`. (reported by @FloorIsTired)
